title: CLSM and SEM Analysis of Extracted Lignin from Walnut Shell (Carya illinoinensis) by Alkaline Treatment
content: Lignin is a very abundant polymer in nature and is present in the cellular structures of several plant species, including wood, agricultural leftovers, and other biopolymeric sources such as pods, shells, nuts, or weeds [1]. This macropolymer has several advantageous characteristics, including antioxidant and biodegradable properties. In addition, after the lignin extraction, it has the potential to be modified and produce other materials such as polymers, carbon fibers, and adhesives, which can be introduced into different sectors [2]. In this sense, the extraction of lignin is essential for the development of sustainable bio-based materials [3]. Various chemical, biological, and mechanical treatments have been used for lignin extraction. However, efficient extraction methods must maintain a good balance between being strong enough to break down the lignin-carbohydrate complexes, and gentle enough to avoid degradation or modification of the carbohydrate polymers. Alkaline treatment is a very efficient method for rupturing ester bonds between lignin, hemicellulose, and cellulose, compared to acidic or oxidative reagents, during the extraction process using alkaline treatment, lignin undergoes a few structural modifications and can be used without the need for purification. Due to these characteristics, lignin is an excellent candidate for chemical modification, which could be used in a variety of applications and give it added value [4]. The main objective of this study was to extract lignin from the walnut shell by alkaline process, using a 5% aqueous NaOH solution. Then, the extracted lignin was characterized by confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and ultraviolet-visible (UV–Vis) techniques.
